replaces: Only the v3 clock proposal's os.uptime source, uptime-ms encoding and review-clock rule. Original reviewed draft remains preserved. All other v3 and retained intent-authority requirements remain.
counterevidence: Independent review inspected exact Node24.22.0 Darwin libuv os.uptime implementation: time(NULL) minus KERN_BOOTTIME, with whole-second granularity. Actual local/child127ms samples left uptime_ms unchanged while hrtime advanced. It is not admitted as the independent monotonic millisecond source proposed in v3.

qualified_source_direction.api: process.hrtime.bigint(), direct unsigned decimal nanoseconds, never process-start subtraction, Number coercion or wall-derived substitute
qualified_source_direction.implementation: Exact Node24.22.0 per_thread.js hrtime.bigint reads the native BigUint64 buffer; node_process_methods.cc stores uv_hrtime directly. Linux UV_CLOCK_PRECISE selects CLOCK_MONOTONIC; Darwin uses mach_continuous_time with the shared timebase.
qualified_source_direction.cross_process: Independent three fresh actual Darwin child observations all had the same boot and parent_before_ns <= child_ns <= parent_after_ns. This supports a shared epoch on that observed host/runtime, not every platform/runtime or container time namespace.
qualified_source_direction.suspend: Darwin continuous time includes suspend; Linux CLOCK_MONOTONIC excludes suspend. Do not assume equal suspend behavior. Dual wall/monotonic lifetime and discrepancy checks apply to review confirmation as well as grant start/resume.
qualified_source_direction.host_gate: Trusted final host must qualify its actual Node/libuv clock fingerprint and same-host/boot shared epoch, plus Linux time namespace when applicable. This turn does not qualify actual Linux execution. Unsupported/unknown runtime, namespace or boot source refuses the dependent operation, with no os.uptime, wall-only or caller-supplied clock fallback.

closed_clock_fields.boot_id: Actual canonical lowercase UUID from fixed Linux boot_id or Darwin kern.bootsessionuuid source
closed_clock_fields.monotonic_ns: Canonical positive decimal string for uint64, at most20 digits and <=18446744073709551615, sampled directly from hrtime.bigint; zero is invalid because a native source failure may return zero. Refuse expiry arithmetic beyond uint64 rather than wrapping.
closed_clock_fields.wall_ms: Integer safe Unix milliseconds from trusted Date.now; no caller override

sampling: Read wall-before, monotonic_ns, actual boot identity, wall-after; require same boot across the trusted host context, nondecreasing wall and wall sample width <=250ms. Store wall-after. Failed observation is refusal, never zero or inferred time.

eligibility.rule: For both review confirmation and new/resumed domain writes: same actual boot/source/context; current wall and monotonic observations cannot precede issue or authenticated predecessor. Monotonic samples must be positive. Require elapsed wall milliseconds and monotonic nanoseconds strictly less than the respective lifetime bounds: equality is expired, preserving v3's before-expiry rule. Absolute elapsed disagreement must be <=2000000000ns after multiplying wall milliseconds by1000000. Compute decimal ns using BigInt only. A boundary/clock/boot failure refuses progression without auto-renewal or inferred completion.
eligibility.sleep_behavior: A long Darwin sleep advances both clocks and is caught by expiry as appropriate; it does not inherently cause disagreement. Linux suspend can produce disagreement because only wall advances. Neither behavior may extend a review/grant past its wall bound.
eligibility.settlement: Expired/revoked complete durable output still follows the retained completion-only matrix with fresh ordinary authority; a clock failure never authorizes new domain outputs or turns partial/uncertain output into completion.

not_delivered: This is a concrete source/encoding correction for independent schema and host implementation. The closed Owner schemas, actual trusted clock reader/namespace binding, review handles, MAC records and actual phase consumer tests remain required before runtime qualification.
